info.title: Micropod API · RigService
info.description:
## micropod.v1.RigService

The rootless rig: which execution mode new workloads use, the shared hvf
 machine's state and lifecycle, and its versioned payload (VMM, kernel,
 initrd, guest tools). The machine is the one MICROPOD_HVF_ROOT names for
 the API process. The REST routes under /v1/rig answer the same data.

post.description:
Activate the staged payload: restart the machine onto it, probe it, and
 return to known-good if it fails. Deferred (`failed_precondition`, nothing
 stopped) while containers run or idleness cannot be confirmed, unless
 `force`.

Start (returns once the guest answers), stop (a stop on request: Ping and
 GetSystem then say stopped and nothing restarts it on demand) or restart
 the machine; replies with its status afterwards. Stop and restart are
 deferred (`failed_precondition`, nothing stopped) while containers run on
 a serving machine or its idleness cannot be confirmed, unless `force`.

What the hvf machine has, what is in use, how hard it is being pushed
 and how many more containers it can take now: the figures a scheduler
 admits work by. One request to the guest engine, which answers from its
 own counters and a once-a-second sample of the kernel's (no subprocess,
 no listing); the Mac's memory pressure is read in this process. Never
 boots anything: unavailable while the machine does not serve.

The machine as every process sees it: assets, supervisor, phase, the
 published state, and its autostart LaunchAgent. Never boots anything;
 while it runs, the guest is asked for its engine version, its
 containers and its cache disk (one second each).

Mode, machine phase, cache disk and policy summary, staged payloads and
 the local dependency proxy (GET /v1/rig/health).

Return to the last known-good payload (POST /v1/rig/hvf/update/rollback),
 deferred like ApplyHVFUpdate.

Turn the machine's autostart LaunchAgent on or off (`micropod machine
 autostart on|off`): on, launchd starts the machine at login and stops it
 cleanly at logout. Loading or unloading the job restarts a running
 machine, so it is deferred (`failed_precondition`, nothing changed)
 while containers run, unless `force`. Replies with the machine status.

Switch mode: container (the shared hvf machine) or sandbox (one micro-VM
 per workload). Writes the default runtime (PUT /v1/rig/mode).

The machine's first run (`micropod setup`): its runtime files from the
 API's own app bundle or CLI package (or `payload_path`), its disk from
 `disk_from` or the package's base disk, and its cache disk; then a start
 when `start`. Local sources only: nothing is downloaded. Re-running
 keeps what is there. A step that cannot be done is a failed step in the
 reply (`ok` false), never a partial install: every source is checked
 before anything is written.

connect-protocol-version.title: Connect-Protocol-Version
connect-protocol-version.description: Define the version of the Connect protocol

code.description: The status code, which should be an enum value of [google.rpc.Code][google.rpc.Code].

message.description: A developer-facing error message, which should be in English. Any user-facing error message should be localized and sent in the [google.rpc.Status.details][google.rpc.Status.details] field, or localized by the client.

details.description: A list of messages that carry the error details. There is no limit on the number of messages.

type.description: A URL that acts as a globally unique identifier for the type of the serialized message. For example: `type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.ErrorInfo`. This is used to determine the schema of the data in the `value` field and is the discriminator for the `debug` field.

value.description: The Protobuf message, serialized as bytes and base64-encoded. The specific message type is identified by the `type` field.

debug.title: Debug
debug.description: Deserialized error detail payload. The 'type' field indicates the schema. This field is for easier debugging and should not be relied upon for application logic.

connect.error_details.Any.description: Contains an arbitrary serialized message along with a @type that describes the type of the serialized message, with an additional debug field for ConnectRPC error details.

force.title: force
force.description: Stop or restart even while containers run (interrupts them).

micropod.v1.Empty.title: Empty
micropod.v1.Empty.description:
The Micropod daemon API is grouped into per-domain services, one per file:

   container.proto — ContainerService (lifecycle, logs, stats, exec)
   image.proto     — ImageService (list, pull, delete)
   volume.proto    — VolumeService (volumes + mount policy)
   network.proto   — NetworkService
   compose.proto   — Compose (up/down over a compose spec)
   system.proto    — SystemService (snapshot, usage, app updates)

 Empty is shared by every service, so it lives here.

force.description: Restart even while containers run (interrupts them).

noop, activated, rolled_back (success); failed_rollback and failed come

sampledUnixMs.description:
When the guest sampled its kernel figures (Unix milliseconds). The
 container counts and the engine's own counters are of the request.

pidMax.title: pid_max
pidMax.description: The most tasks (processes and threads) the guest kernel runs at once.

maxContainers.title: max_containers
maxContainers.description: The most containers running at once the headroom is counted against.

familyContainersMax.description: The most containers one delegated Docker socket may hold at once.

relayConnectionsMax.title: relay_connections_max
relayConnectionsMax.description:
The most gateway relay connections (published ports reached from
 containers) the engine holds at once.

cacheDisk.title: cache_disk
cacheDisk.description: Unset when the machine has no cache disk.

micropod.v1.MachineCapacity.title: MachineCapacity
micropod.v1.MachineCapacity.description: The hvf machine's capacity, load and headroom (GetMachineCapacity).

requestedMilliCpu.title: requested_milli_cpu
requestedMilliCpu.description:
The CPU limits (thousandths of a CPU) and memory limits of the running
 and starting containers, summed; without_cpu_limit counts those with no
 CPU limit, which the sum leaves out, as it does a memory limit of the
 whole machine.

families.title: families
families.description:
By family, the largest first, at most 64 rows (the rest summed as
 "(other)"). A family is a delegated Docker socket's owner and what it
 created, named by the owner's io.micropod.family label or its name; or
 every container the host created with the same io.micropod.family
 label; "" is what the host created without one.

startP50Ms.title: start_p50_ms
startP50Ms.description:
Over the latest starts_sampled starts (256 at most): from the start
 request to the container's process running, in milliseconds.

reasons.title: reasons
reasons.description: Why it is under pressure; empty when it is not.

limitedBy.title: limited_by
limitedBy.description:
The resource containers is the smallest for: cpu, memory, tasks,
 containers, os-disk, cache-disk, pressure or host-memory.

micropod.v1.MachineHeadroom.title: MachineHeadroom
micropod.v1.MachineHeadroom.description:
How many more typical containers the machine can take now.

 The unit is one typical container: what the running ones use on average
 (busy CPUs / running, used memory / running), held to 0.25..2 CPUs and
 256 MiB..4 GiB; 0.5 CPU and 512 MiB when nothing runs.

   by_cpu        = (cpus * 0.90 - busy CPUs) / unit_cpu
   by_memory     = (memory available - max(5% of memory, 1 GiB)) / unit_memory_bytes
   by_tasks      = (pid_max * 0.80 - tasks) / 64
   by_containers = max_containers - containers running or starting
   containers    = max(0, the smallest of the four)

 and 0 under pressure: memory PSI some avg10 >= 10 or full avg10 >= 2, CPU
 PSI some avg10 >= 80, IO PSI full avg10 >= 25, less memory available than
 the reserve, a disk with less than max(5%, 2 GiB) free, a start-latency
 p95 of 10 s or more, or the Mac itself under memory pressure (warning or
 critical). CPU and memory are counted on what is used, not on the limits
 containers were given: a limit is a ceiling, and the pressure terms catch
 a machine whose promised memory is being used after all.

memoryAvailableBytes.title: memory_available_bytes
memoryAvailableBytes.description: Free, inactive, speculative and purgeable memory.

memoryPressure.title: memory_pressure
memoryPressure.description:
normal, warning or critical (the kernel's memory pressure level); empty
 when it could not be read.

micropod.v1.MachineHost.title: MachineHost
micropod.v1.MachineHost.description: The Mac the machine runs on, read by the API process.

micropod.v1.MachinePressure.title: MachinePressure
micropod.v1.MachinePressure.description:
The guest kernel's pressure stall information: the percentage of the last
 10, 60 and 300 seconds in which some, or all, tasks were stalled on a
 resource. available is false on a kernel without it.

cpuBusyFraction.title: cpu_busy_fraction
cpuBusyFraction.description:
The share of all CPUs busy over the second before the sample (0..1),
 and the same as a number of CPUs.

runnable.title: runnable
runnable.description: Tasks runnable now, and all tasks.

configured.title: configured
configured.description: The host has caches.ext4, so the VMM attaches it.

missing.title: missing
missing.description: machine.json expects a cache disk that is gone.

source.title: source
source.description: guest, or unknown when the guest did not answer.

unavailable.title: unavailable
unavailable.description: Why shared caches are off this boot.

micropod.v1.RigCacheDisk.title: RigCacheDisk
micropod.v1.RigCacheDisk.description:
The cache disk as rig health reports it: the guest's account when it
 answered, else why it is unknown.

dockerSocket.title: docker_socket
dockerSocket.description:
trusted or any: which containers may be given a Docker socket
 (CachePolicy.docker_socket as the guest applies it).

defaultLimits.title: default_limits
defaultLimits.description:
job or none: what a container naming no limit gets
 (CachePolicy.default_limits as the guest applies it).

phase.title: phase
phase.description: starting, running, stopping, stopped or failed.

configError.title: config_error
configError.description: machine.json did not load: the policy summary shows the defaults' values.

mode.title: mode
mode.description: The active mode, or the default runtime's name when it maps to no mode.

engine.title: engine
engine.description: The engine the mode runs on (hvf, sandbox).

force.title: force
force.description: Restart a machine that runs containers (interrupts them).

mode.title: mode
mode.description: container or sandbox (an engine name is accepted too).

payloadPath.title: payload_path

diskFrom.title: disk_from
diskFrom.description:
A local ext4 image the disk is cloned (or copied) from; empty: the
 package's base disk.

cacheDiskBytes.title: cache_disk_bytes
cacheDiskBytes.description: The cache disk's size; 0: 32 GiB for a new machine.

noCacheDisk.title: no_cache_disk
noCacheDisk.description: No cache disk: the dependency caches live on the OS disk.

start.title: start
start.description: Boot the machine once it is installed (returns once the guest answers).

id.title: id
id.description: runtime-files, disk, cache-disk, start or default-runtime.

state.title: state
state.description:
done, kept (already there), skipped (not asked for), failed, or pending
 (not reached: an earlier step failed).

detail.title: detail
detail.description: What it did, or why it failed.
